svg.title: What every shape, colour and line style in this atlas means
svg.desc: The key to the other eight figures. Colour carries who owns a thing: indigo for a person, blue for something in the visitor's browser or at the edge, green for code this repository owns and runs, amber for a check that is allowed to reject, grey for a third party, red for regulated data under the ten-year retention obligation, violet for a stored artifact such as a secret, a parameter or a bucket. Shape carries what kind of thing it is: a rounded stadium is a person, a rectangle is a process or a component, a hexagon is a gate, a double rectangle is a container or a document that runs, a cylinder is stored data, and a parallelogram is a scheduled or external trigger. Line style carries what happens: a plain arrow is normal flow, a thick arrow is the answer coming back, a crossed arrow is a path that is refused or deliberately absent, and a dotted arrow is something that happens out of band rather than during the request. A red line is drawn wherever the thing being refused is the point of the figure.
